metadata.title: Young People’s Civic Attitudes and Practices: England’s Outcomes from the IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study (ICCS)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report is based on the ICCS 2009 main survey administered in England to Year 9 pupils (13–14 years old), with data cleaned and processed by the IEA Data Processing Center (DPC) and then analysed by NFER. The ICCS framework describes that DPC computed weights according to an approved sampling design after data cleaning, and national datasets were provided for country-level analyses. However, this England national report does not specify the exact weight variable name(s) or whether the subsequent national multilevel modelling analyses explicitly applied those weights. Because the study is primarily a descriptive/national reporting report using multilevel modelling rather than machine-learning prediction, the manuscript does not provide enough detail to confirm whether complex survey weights were applied in the reported modelling results.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report does not present a machine-learning analysis of cognitive achievement using ICCS/PV-style plausible values. Instead, it reports ICCS cognitive scale scores derived from Rasch models (and questionnaire-based attitudinal scales) and uses multilevel modelling to examine associations between these outcomes and background/context variables. As a result, plausible-value handling is not applicable to the reported outcomes, and the manuscript also does not document a missing-data strategy for the multilevel modelling analyses (e.g., listwise deletion vs imputation), representing a reporting gap.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report presents England national-level findings from ICCS 2009, using England’s national dataset. The ICCS main survey in England was conducted between late February and early April 2009 with Year 9 pupils (average age 14.0). The report states that the ICCS consortium applied sampling participation and exclusion standards (e.g., exclusions not exceeding 5% of the national desired target population), and that DPC cleaned and checked datasets prior to computing weights. No additional analytic inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., complete-case only, specific missingness thresholds, or task-level filters) are explicitly described for the multilevel modelling results in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This DfE report uses ICCS 2009 England (Year 9) data to describe pupils’ civic knowledge and attitudes and to model associations between these outcomes and pupil, home, and school factors using multilevel modelling. The report finds that civic knowledge is a strong predictor of positive democratic values, gender equality attitudes, and support for equal rights for ethnic groups and immigrants, while some classroom and school ethos variables show mixed directions (e.g., pupil influence at school is negatively associated with civic knowledge). For gender equality, normalized coefficients are reported for civic knowledge (37.5), being female (28.1), and openness in class discussion (8.2). For in-school participation, normalized coefficients are reported for civic knowledge (17.0), home literacy (14.9), parent interest (13.1), and openness (10.2), and for future voting intention civic knowledge (29.7) and parent interest (25.3). No machine-learning algorithms are evaluated, and the report does not provide a missing-data handling strategy for the modelling results.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
